# Guideline-driven escalation toward statin-plus-ezetimibe

The Lipid Association of India recommends achieving additional LDL-cholesterol
reduction through **high-intensity statin therapy combined with add-on
ezetimibe**, followed where necessary by PCSK9 inhibitors. The LAI's 2020
consensus positions ezetimibe first in the escalation sequence, then PCSK9
inhibitors and bempedoic acid, for patients needing more aggressive lowering.

The Association also notes explicitly that **ezetimibe and bempedoic acid are
only moderately more expensive than statins**, which is the economic argument
that makes the escalation realistic in the Indian market rather than
theoretical.

LAI has separately published proposed LDL-C goals for secondary prevention and
familial hypercholesterolaemia in India, setting targets that a statin alone
frequently cannot reach.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

Guideline escalation is the most reliable predictor of a decade-long shift in
prescribing mix. When the recommended next step after a maximally tolerated
statin is ezetimibe, the fixed-dose statin-plus-ezetimibe combination becomes
the natural commercial expression of that guidance - one prescription instead of
two, better adherence, and a defensible premium over plain statin.

This is the strongest single external tailwind in the corpus and is applied
directly to the ezetimibe-anchored molecule cluster.
